paper_sections.title: Altered regional activity and connectivity of functional brain networks in congenital unilateral conductive hearing loss
Differences in regional activity and connectivity
Ethics approval and consent to participate

description.value: The study investigated altered regional spontaneous activity and seed-based functional connectivity in patients with congenital right-sided unilateral microtia and severe conductive hearing loss, and examined associations with hearing and clinical variables, with and without global signal regression.

design.value: A cross-sectional resting-state fMRI study comparing 24 patients with congenital right-sided unilateral microtia with 25 age- and sex-matched normal-hearing controls. Regional activity was assessed using ALFF, fALFF and ReHo, and seed-based functional connectivity was assessed using clusters showing between-group differences. Analyses were performed with and without global signal regression.

description.value: Hearing level was assessed in a closed field at six frequencies (0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8 kHz).
Cognitive abilities were evaluated by professionals using the Mini-Mental State Examination.
Cognitive abilities were evaluated by professionals using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment test.
27 patients aged 11–40 years with right-sided congenital unilateral microtia; finally, 24 patients with UM were included.

description.value: Functional images were obtained axially with a gradient echo type echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence. Parameters included 36 slices, 4 mm thickness, 0 mm gap, 64 × 64 acquisition matrix, 90° flip angle, 200 × 200 mm² FOV, and 3.75 × 3.75 × 4 mm³ voxel size.

pulse_sequence_type.value: gradient echo type echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence

description.value: Anatomical images were acquired with a high-resolution T1-weighted gradient-echo sequence; TR 7.9 ms, TE 2.9 ms, flip angle 7°, thickness 1 mm, 192 slices, FOV 256 × 256 mm², voxel size 1 × 1 × 1 mm³.

Resting-state fMRI images were processed using SPM12 and SeeCAT. The first 10 time points were deleted; slice-timing and head-motion correction were implemented; images were normalized to the EPI template, resampled to 3-mm isotropic voxels, smoothed with a 4-mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian kernel, nuisance signals were regressed, time series were band-pass filtered, and scrubbing was performed.

steps.value: The first 10 time points of the functional imaging were deleted.
Slice-timing and head-motion correction were implemented.
The corrected images were normalized to the EPI template.
Smoothed with a 4-mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian kernel.
Confounding signals, including white matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals, linear drift and Friston-24 head-motion parameters, were removed using a linear regression model.
Volumes with >0.5 mm framewise displacement and adjacent volumes were replaced using linear interpolated data.

description.value: rs-fMRI data were analyzed both with and without global signal regression during preprocessing.

steps.value: Global signal regression uses linear regression to remove the global signal from the time series of each voxel.

model_settings.value: ALFF, fALFF, ReHo and SBFC were compared in the two groups with regression of age, gender and educational level as covariates. Gaussian random field corrections used p < 0.001 at the voxel level and p < 0.05 at the cluster level.

ROI-wise Pearson’s correlation analysis investigated relationships between brain regions showing group differences and clinical features. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05 with the Bonferroni correction.
